name: com.loopxxi/loop-mcp
title: loop-mcp
description: 17 Bitcoin, business, data and developer tools for AI agents; 7 paid per call over Lightning (L402).

tools.name: btc_price
tools.description: Get the current Bitcoin spot price in USD, EUR, GBP, CAD, CHF, AUD and JPY. Use it to convert between BTC or sats and fiat, or to quote a price; for whether to broadcast now use btc_send_decision, and for fee timing use optimal_send_window. Takes no input. Read-only: each call makes one live HTTPS read of mempool.space; the result is not stored. Returns the upstream object as served (time in Unix seconds, one whole-unit price per currency) plus source (the URL read), fetched_at (UTC, RFC 3339) and source_sha256 (SHA-256 of the upstream body). Returns an upstream error if mempool.space is unreachable or sends invalid JSON. Price: 10 sats per call.

tools.name: btc_send_decision
tools.description: Returns a composited send-or-wait recommendation for a Bitcoin transaction. Fetches live mempool and fee data, then outputs a machine-actionable verdict (SEND_NOW, WAIT, or URGENT_ONLY) with fee rates in sat/vB, mempool pressure level, and estimated savings if you wait. Ideal for agents that need a single decision call instead of parsing multiple raw mempool endpoints. Price: 15 sats per call.

tools.description: Resolve a Lightning Address (user@domain.com) to a payable BOLT11 invoice for a given amount. Handles the full LNURL-pay protocol internally. Returns the invoice plus min/max sendable amounts for validation. Price: 10 sats per call.

tools.name: tx_decode_explain
tools.description: Fetch a Bitcoin transaction by txid and return a structured, agent-ready summary: type (P2WPKH/P2TR/P2SH/etc.), input/output counts, fees, fee rate in sat/vB, confirmation status, RBF flag, SegWit/Taproot flags, and a one-line agent_summary string ready for LLM context injection. Saves 500-2000 tokens vs parsing raw TX JSON. Price: 25 sats per call.

tools.name: optimal_send_window
tools.description: Bitcoin transaction timing intelligence. Returns a congestion forecast for the next 1-4h, a recommended UTC send window when fees are projected at/below your target, a fee trajectory (rising/stable/falling) with a calibrated confidence score, next-block minimum fee, confirmation targets for 3/6/144 blocks, and an RBF-viability flag. A synthesis layer above raw fee data — the decision an autonomous payment agent needs before broadcasting. Source: mempool.space. Price: 25 sats per call.

hours_ahead.description: How far ahead to search for the optimal window (1-6h, default 4).

tools.name: json_validate
tools.description: Validate JSON text, identify its root type, and return compact normalized JSON (object keys sorted) plus a SHA-256 hash of it. Use it to check model or API output before parsing, or to compare two documents by hash; to read one field use json_extract. Runs without network access and does not store your input. Input up to 100,000 bytes (larger input is an error); trailing data after the first value counts as invalid. Returns valid, root_type, normalized_json, bytes and sha256; invalid JSON returns valid false with the parser error instead of failing. normalized_json escapes <, > and & as \u003c, \u003e and \u0026, and sha256 is the hash of that string.

tools.name: text_analyze
tools.description: Return deterministic text statistics: bytes, characters, words, lines, sentences, estimated_tokens (characters / 4, rounded up), reading_minutes (at 200 words per minute) and a SHA-256 hash of the exact text. Use it to size text against a context or length limit, or to fingerprint it; counts are heuristics, not a model tokenizer. Runs without network access and does not store your input. Input up to 100,000 bytes; larger input is an error.

tools.name: hash_generate
tools.description: Generate a SHA-256 or SHA-512 digest of UTF-8 text in hexadecimal or Base64 form. Use it for checksums, cache keys or comparing content; it is a plain digest, not a keyed HMAC or a password hash. Runs without network access and does not store your input. Input up to 100,000 bytes; larger input is an error. Returns algorithm, encoding, digest and bytes (input length). Defaults: sha256, hex; any other algorithm or encoding is an error.

tools.name: base64_convert
tools.description: Encode UTF-8 text to Base64, or decode Base64, with the standard or URL-safe alphabet. Use it for data URIs, HTTP headers or token segments; to read a JWT use jwt_decode. Runs without network access and does not store your input. Input up to 100,000 bytes; larger input is an error. Encode returns base64 and bytes; URL-safe output has no padding. Decode accepts padded or unpadded input and returns text when the bytes are valid UTF-8, otherwise text null plus hex. Invalid Base64 is an error.

tools.name: timestamp_convert
tools.description: Convert Unix seconds, Unix milliseconds, RFC 3339 or a YYYY-MM-DD date into normalized UTC forms. Use it to compare or store times from different APIs or logs; output is always UTC, with no conversion to other time zones. With from auto (default), an integer of 13 or more digits is read as milliseconds, a shorter one as seconds, and YYYY-MM-DD as a UTC date. Runs without network access and does not store your input. Returns input_format, rfc3339, unix, unix_ms, date_utc, time_utc and weekday; an unparseable value is an error.

tools.name: business_ratios
tools.description: Compute cash runway in months, cash buffer days, current ratio, quick ratio, debt to equity, DSO, DIO, DPO and cash conversion cycle from any subset of a business's own cash, monthly flow and balance sheet figures. Arithmetic only, no network. Each value carries its formula and the inputs it used; a value that cannot be computed is null with a reason. Use it to check a company's liquidity, leverage or working-capital cycle from figures you already have; it does not fetch filings or market data. All inputs are optional numbers in one currency unit (monthly figures per month, annual figures for the last twelve months); pass only what you know. Returns inputs, ratios (each with value, unit, formula, inputs and, when null, reason), rounded_to_decimals (4) and about (provider, contact, description). Same input, same output. Price: 10 sats per call.

tools.name: l402_recheck
tools.description: Endpoint operators and buyers can check one listed L402 endpoint by passing its id from the newest Agent Payments Index probe file. One live request gives the buyer a private result with the current status, the challenge and invoice amount, and the last daily result for comparison. An endpoint timeout or error is charged. Rate limits are checked before an invoice is issued, but a paid call can still be refused later. If the failure is ours, your Lightning payment has already settled and there is no automatic refund. The macaroon and invoice string are never returned and results are not published. Price: 21 sats per call.

id.description: Endpoint id from the newest Agent Payments Index probe file, listed at https://loopxxi.com/agent-payments-index/hosts.
